ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Electrostatic field focusing plays an important role in electron microscopes and oscilloscope tubes. The figure shows the focusing electric field inside a certain oscilloscope tube; the solid lines and dashed lines respectively represent electric field lines and equipotential lines. Two electrons move from points a and b respectively to point c, then (    )
A. The focusing electric field always does negative work on the two electrons
B. The electric potential energy that the electron has at point a is smaller than that at point b
C. The electric potential at point a is lower than that at point c
D. The electric field strength at b is smaller than that at c

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Electrostatic field focusing plays an important role in electron microscopes and oscilloscope tubes. The figure shows the focusing electric field inside a certain oscilloscope tube; the solid lines and dashed lines respectively represent electric field lines and equipotential lines. Two electrons move from points a and b respectively to point c. According to the figure, how does the electric potential at point a compare with that at point c?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The electric potential at point a is lower than that at point c
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are solid lines and dashed lines in the figure, and the problem statement explains that the solid lines represent electric field lines and the dashed lines represent equipotential lines. Point c is located on the right side of the figure, and point a is located near the upper left. Observing the arrows on the solid lines, the arrows of the electric field lines from near c on the right side to near a on the upper left are roughly from right to left, pointing from the region where c is located to the region where a is located. Reasoning: Electric potential gradually decreases along the direction of the electric field lines. Since the electric field direction is roughly from c toward a, then when going from c to a along the direction of the electric field, the electric potential decreases, so the electric potential at point a is less than the electric potential at point c, that is, Va < Vc.
